parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the need for a pure Node.js ESM port, manual CLI parsing, PyYAML load/dump behavior, `/output` files, and no external modules, JSON, or regular expressions.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent wrote a shared behavior spec and type file, then delegated `argparse.mjs`, `yamlParser.mjs`, and `yamlDumper.mjs` to three children; no child or parent step owned `test4.mjs` final assembly.
parallel.implementation: Argparse was implemented and heavily checked by one child. Parser and dumper children each wrote large module files, but neither completed its own test/report cycle before cancellation.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final tree contained `SPEC.md`, `yamlTypes.mjs`, `argparse.mjs`, `yamlParser.mjs`, and `yamlDumper.mjs`, but no entry point, no integrated wrapper, and no assembled runnable program.
parallel.verification: The argparse child reported 52 differential checks, while parser and dumper had only exploratory probes and no completed self-verification; the parent ran no whole-program check.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with two failed child results and no `test4.mjs`; official evaluation completed and scored 0 of 146.

serial.requirements: The single agent recognized the same CLI, YAML load/dump, ESM, no-dependency, no-JSON, no-RegExp, output, and final entry requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial agent kept ownership local and created a staged todo list covering base modules, scanner, parser, constructor, emitter, `yaml.mjs`, `argparse.mjs`, `test4.mjs`, and comparison testing.
serial.implementation: It wrote `pycompat.mjs`, `nodes.mjs`, `reader.mjs`, `tokens.mjs`, `scanner.mjs`, `resolver.mjs`, `parser.mjs`, and `constructor.mjs`, but did not reach the dumper/emitter, CLI parser, wrapper, or entry.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No delegated integration was needed, but the local implementation stopped before assembling a runnable program or placing `test4.mjs` in the final output.
serial.verification: It ran many black-box reference probes and some module import checks while developing, but no final differential harness or official-like whole-program verification completed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out during the next planned step, artifact validation lacked `test4.mjs`, and official evaluation completed with 0 of 146.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full Py2JS task and generated a child-facing spec, but its child briefs carried a stale original-source path and did not allocate the final entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the full task directly from the prompt and retained the final entry in its local plan, but did not reach it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both understood the core behavior; parallel transformed requirements through child briefs and lost some environment and delivery context, while serial kept the whole requirement set in one workflow.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into three child-owned modules after parent setup, with children prohibited from modifying other files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one owner with a staged todo list for base modules, parser, constructor, emitter, wrapper, CLI parser, entry, and final harness.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained concurrent module work but left final assembly unowned; serial had slower local progress but a coherent owner for the end-to-end deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent observed the actual dataset layout, but delegated stale `/workspace/dataset/yaml/test4.py` instructions and only module-level ownership contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked directly against the prompt and executable path with no inter-agent handoff or child interface boundary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a brief-to-child context boundary with a wrong source path and no final entry contract; serial avoided that boundary but still ran out of time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a shared spec/type file and three module files: one completed argparse module and two large YAML modules from children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a larger set of low-level parser-related modules but did not get to dumper, CLI parser, wrapper, or entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel made more horizontal module progress, while serial made deeper parser infrastructure progress; neither produced the runnable top-level program.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent received the argparse child result, but parser and dumper children were stopped and returned failed child results at cancellation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; its own main turn was interrupted while still working through planned modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child completion and cancellation lifecycle risks; serial failed through single-agent unfinished work rather than unjoined or cancelled child results.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to the same `/output` tree but to separate intended module files; no overwrite was shown, yet no integrated runnable tree was assembled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote directly to `/output/lib` with a single owner and no shared-write collision, but also never assembled the runnable tree.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shared state was not collision-contaminated; the material integration gap was absence of final assembly. Serial's integration gap was simply unfinished local work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Argparse was checked by one child, but parser/dumper had no completed child verification and the parent ran no end-to-end acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran many black-box probes and a few import checks during implementation, but no full final harness or evaluator-aligned run completed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification was fragmented by child ownership and cut off for YAML modules; serial verification was local and exploratory but also incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full budget waiting on three children, then cancelled two active child steps and the parent step.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed the full budget in one long main-agent implementation path and was cancelled in step 31.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both timed out, but the parallel closure involved child cancellations and failed child results, while serial closure was one unfinished local continuation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official current status evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial completed official evaluation and failed 0 of 146. The concrete task-solving difference is that parallel spread module work across three children and produced some module side effects, but missed final entry assembly and lost parser/dumper children to cancellation; serial kept the whole plan local and explicitly planned the entry file, but timed out before reaching the final modules and entry.
parallel_contributors: Parallel omitted a final assembly owner for `test4.mjs` while constraining children to module-only scopes.
Parallel children were given a stale source path that caused avoidable recovery work.
Parallel parser and dumper children were cancelled before completed handoffs or verification.
serial_contributors: Serial kept the whole task in one long local path and did not complete the later dumper, CLI, wrapper, entry, or final harness stages.
Serial artifact validation also missed `test4.mjs`, so the official score was 0 of 146.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial wrote lower-level scanner/parser/constructor infrastructure rather than separate parser and dumper modules.
Parallel's argparse module was more completely verified than any serial CLI parser because serial never reached the CLI parser stage.
